To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the electrode potentials for metals in a vacuum arc, i.e. the values of the cathode fall across the metal plasma interfaces, are of the same magnitude (and, in fact, comparable values) as the energies of the plasmon modes of the metal plasma interfaces.

the interfacial potential drops across a metal plasma interface (i.e. the cathodic drop) and the interfacial energy of the plasma wave at the interface (i.e the plasmon energy) are of the same magnitude and that the two are related by a simple proportionality constant which is a function only of the plasma parameters.
the electrode potentials of the thirty two metals, for which data are available in the literature, are equal to their interfacial plasm on energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interphasic region between a metal and a gaseous plasma.
the electrode potential and the interfacial energy associated with the metal/gas interface.

the study of the metal/plasma interface in the vacuum arc, and its characterization in terms of electrode potentials and interfacial plasmatic excitations, and the implications of these findings in relation to the cathode erosion processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrode potential is nothing but the interfacial plasma wave energy.
the cathode fall is a measure of the interfacialelectrode potential and the interfacial plasma wave frequency.
the cathodic interface in the arc behaves like a metal gaseous electrolytic interface, and that the cathode potential drop is the interfacial potential across the metal plasma interphase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrode potential of a metal is a measure of the energy of the interfacially confined plasmons.
the electrode potential of a metal is a characteristic property of the metal which is associated with the interfacial plasma wave.
the cathode fall is the electrode potential of the cathode in a metal plasma interface and is equal to the interfacial plasma energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrode potential is an interfacial plasmic property and not just a surface property as has been the case so far.
electrode potentials are associated with the interface plasmons at the metal plasma boundary.
the metal plasma interfacial potential is of the same order as the interfacially confined plasma energy.
